description.narrative:
The most significant expected project-level outcomes are derived from increased access to quality digital connectivity for individuals and businesses, by supporting broadband network expansion and upgrade through investment in core network, transmission and IP infrastructures in Senegal, as well as a potential cross-border acquisition. Further, the Project is also expected to increase access to digital literacy and skills training for individuals by supporting the expansion of a series of digital training and skills development programs that have the potential to enable higher access to and usage of the Internet by individuals, including women, youth and tech entrepreneurs in Senegal.
Beyond the project, the main sources of Market Creation impact are derived from stronger integration of capital markets in West Africa by strengthening financial market linkages via demonstration and replication of an innovative instrument. This transaction is introducing, for the first time in the region, a securitization instrument to mobilize resources at scale for the telecom sector. A successful issuance of the securities is expected to demonstrate its effectiveness in the telecom sector and induce replication by other operators, thereby contributing to deepening capital markets across the target countries, especially in Senegal. This investment also has the potential to sustain the competitiveness of the market for mobile connectivity across the target countries, especially in Senegal, by supporting further expansion of high-speed mobile internet by a large player.

The proposed IFC financing consists of: (i) A senior, unsecured loan comprising an A Loan in the amount of up to 37 million equivalent in local currency to the Company, for IFCs own account, and B1 Loan under IFCs standard B Loan program and/or Parallel loans to the Company mobilized or Parallel loans, for the account of participants or Parallel lenders, in the amount of up to 50 million equivalent in local currency to be structured as Sustainability-Linked Financing (SLF); and (ii) an up to XOF25 billion (approximately 38 million equivalent) investment in an up to XOF75 billion (approximately 114 million equivalent) of tranche C1 and tranche C2 XOF-denominated asset-backed securities (ABS or Securitization), issued by a Fonds Commun de Titrisation de Créances (FCTC). IFC will act as an anchor investor and subscribe to up to 33.3 percent of the total issuance across the two tranches. The project is expected to be supported by the IDA20 Private Sector Window Local Currency Facility (IDA20 PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
